episode.title: Adapt heterogeneous provider errors into actionable HTTP failure messages
episode.before: At parent 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053, provider catch paths generally used only Error.message or JSON.stringify(error). Consequently, gateway or proxy failures whose SDK objects retained the HTTP body in fields such as error.error or error.$response.body surfaced opaque text such as "403 status code (no body)" or "Unknown: UnknownError". Status-prefixed response adapters preserved status but still omitted separately stored response bodies.
episode.after: At merge commit 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46, a shared adapter extracts status and body data from several SDK error shapes, safely serializes non-Error throws, rejects empty bodies, caps body text at 4000 characters, and records whether the existing message already contains the body. Shared formatting then surfaces status plus body without duplicating an already-complete message. Eight text/image/response provider catch paths use the adapter; the Bedrock path retains its exception-category and data-retention behavior while selecting normalized body content, and the completions path avoids appending metadata already present in the normalized output.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053, the implementation adds packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts, updates eight provider adapters, and adds three test files. The merge reports 580 insertions and 36 deletions across 12 files. The core change replaces message-only error handling with normalization and formatting of SDK-specific status/body fields, adds bounded and duplicate-aware output behavior, and exercises helper-level edge cases plus real catch paths for image generation, completions, responses, and Bedrock streaming.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit resolves PR/issue 5832 with subject "fix(ai): surface provider HTTP error body instead of opaque SDK message" and has first parent 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053 and implementation parent 62fad94f1ab17e94a3f6f8d00ef3bae5cd5f8f66.
The first-parent diff modifies eight provider API adapters, adds one shared error-body utility, and adds three test files; the commit stat is 580 insertions and 36 deletions across 12 files.
evidence_units.source: git diff --name-status 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46 -- packages/ai/src packages/ai/test; git show --stat 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46

evidence_units.claim: The shared normalizer maps SDK-specific status fields statusCode, status, $metadata.httpStatusCode, and $response.statusCode into one optional numeric status, and maps body, non-empty error objects, and $response.body into one body string.

Normalization safely serializes non-Error throws, trims and rejects empty body text, truncates retained bodies to 4000 characters, and marks when the original message already contains the extracted body.

The formatter preserves the original message when it already carries the body or when status/body data is incomplete; otherwise it emits status and body, optionally retaining a provider-specific prefix.

Before the change, the response adapters formatted Error.message and optional status directly, while the other affected catch paths assigned Error.message or JSON.stringify(error); none consulted parsed or raw SDK body fields.
evidence_units.source: git diff 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46 -- packages/ai/src/api/azure-openai-responses.ts packages/ai/src/api/bedrock-converse-stream.ts packages/ai/src/api/google-generative-ai.ts packages/ai/src/api/google-vertex.ts packages/ai/src/api/openai-codex-responses.ts packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts packages/ai/src/api/openrouter-images.ts

evidence_units.claim: Azure responses, Google generative and vertex streams, Codex responses, completions, OpenAI responses, and image generation route caught values through normalizeProviderError and formatProviderError; response adapters supply their existing API-specific prefixes.
The Bedrock formatter uses normalized status/body content only when the SDK message did not already carry the body, while preserving service-exception prefixes and the existing data-retention hint.
The completions catch path appends provider-specific metadata.raw only when the normalized error message does not already contain it.

Helper tests cover status/body extraction for multiple SDK shapes, preservation of messages that already contain a body, non-Error serialization, empty parsed objects, truncation, prefixed formatting, and unprefixed formatting.

An image-provider regression test injects an opaque 403 SDK error carrying a parsed body and requires the returned errorMessage to contain both 403 and the gateway reason rather than equal the opaque SDK message.
Representative catch-path tests require completions, prefixed responses, and Bedrock streaming to surface status plus body, and require provider metadata.raw to appear exactly once.

The available evidence bundle identifies repository earendil-works/pi, issue/PR 5832, and the title "surface provider HTTP error body instead of opaque SDK message", but records the issue body, comments, timeline, reviews, and status checks as unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: Normalize heterogeneous SDK error envelopes
candidate_atomics.description: Adapt an unknown thrown value into a common status/body/message contract by probing known transport fields, safely serializing fallback values, rejecting empty bodies, bounding body length, and recording whether the message already contains the body.

semantic_action.intent: Recover actionable HTTP failure details that remain present in provider SDK error objects but are absent from their display messages.
semantic_action.pre_state: A provider request has thrown an unknown value whose status and response body may be stored under SDK-specific fields or whose value may not be an Error.
semantic_action.post_state: The value is represented as a bounded normalized record containing a stable message, optional numeric status, optional non-empty body, and a duplicate-detection flag.
semantic_action.validation: Helper tests synthesize multiple SDK envelopes and edge cases and assert extracted status/body, safe fallback serialization, empty-body handling, truncation, and messageCarriesBody behavior.

candidate_atomics.name: Compose a duplicate-aware provider error message
candidate_atomics.description: Render a normalized failure so separately retained HTTP details are exposed, while preserving already-complete messages and optional adapter-specific prefixes.

semantic_action.intent: Replace opaque SDK messages with useful status-and-body output without printing a response body twice or discarding established prefixes.
semantic_action.pre_state: A normalized provider error contains a message and may contain status, body, and evidence that the message already carries the body.
semantic_action.post_state: The display string contains status plus body when both were separately recovered; otherwise it preserves the original message, adding an established prefix and status where applicable.
semantic_action.validation: Formatter tests assert unprefixed and prefixed status/body output, preservation of a message that already carries its body, and bare fallback formatting for non-Error values.

candidate_atomics.name: Route provider catch paths through the shared adapter
candidate_atomics.description: Replace message-only error extraction across affected request adapters with the shared normalization and formatting contract while leaving abort/error stop-state behavior intact.

semantic_action.intent: Make text, response, and image request surfaces consistently expose recoverable HTTP response reasons.
semantic_action.pre_state: Affected catch paths derive errorMessage only from Error.message, String, or JSON.stringify and therefore omit bodies retained in SDK-specific fields.
semantic_action.post_state: Affected catch paths derive errorMessage through the shared normalized contract, with existing response prefixes preserved where configured.
semantic_action.validation: Mocked provider-path tests inject opaque 403 errors with separately stored bodies and assert that image generation, completions, and response streaming return error state containing both status and body reason.

candidate_atomics.name: Reconcile provider-specific error decorations
candidate_atomics.description: Preserve specialized exception labels and hints, but prevent auxiliary provider metadata from duplicating content already surfaced by normalization.

semantic_action.intent: Retain useful adapter-specific error context while avoiding duplicate diagnostic text after introducing shared body extraction.
semantic_action.pre_state: An adapter has extra error decorations, such as exception-category prefixes, guidance hints, or metadata.raw, in addition to the normalized HTTP body.
semantic_action.post_state: Specialized prefixes and hints remain available, and auxiliary raw metadata is appended only when absent from the normalized message.
semantic_action.validation: Regression tests assert Bedrock exposes the gateway body instead of the opaque Unknown error and that completions output contains metadata.raw exactly once.

candidate_workflows.name: Adapt provider failures without losing response-body diagnostics
candidate_workflows.description: Use when multiple provider SDKs encode HTTP failures differently and catch paths expose only opaque messages. Do not replace already-useful messages unconditionally, duplicate body or metadata content, remove existing provider prefixes/hints, or emit unbounded response bodies. Establish a normalized error contract, format it conditionally, integrate it at request failure boundaries, reconcile provider-specific decorations, and validate both helpers and representative end-to-end catch paths.
